findings.location: Definition, Cellular structure and Explicit normalization of the semistandard maps; frontmatter justified_by: []
findings.evidence: The Hom/intersection basis theorem, semistandard cellularity and nonzero Weyl heads are asserted without local proofs or proved well-definedness suppliers. The declared dependencies do not establish these q-Schur constructions. Needed: local Hom/intersection and cellular-basis proofs, followed by the canonical projection norm-one argument. The missing construction corresponds to [Mathas](https://web.math.ucsb.edu/~bigelow/books/mathas.pdf), Theorems 4.8, 4.10 and 4.14; citation alone does not discharge the active local-proof obligation.

findings.location: Proof 1.4, intersection factorial/residual row-ideal assertion and preservation of canonical rows; Proof 4.1
findings.evidence: The proof needs an explicit parabolic-intersection factorization yielding [beta]!_Q, membership of the remaining sum in the specified residual row ideal, and straightening preserving the first j canonical rows. F5 supplies row action and Murphy straightening, but no such row-entry divisibility lemma. These assertions are essential to the finite-e zero-label implication. Needed: the complete integral factorization and fixed-row support argument corresponding to Mathas Lemma 3.38.

findings.location: Proof 2.1, definitions of U_T, V_T and pi_t and the asserted scalar and leading-coefficient identities
findings.evidence: The adjoint cross-weight maps are not specified as actual Schur endomorphisms. Their first-standardization scalar and leading coefficient are asserted without computation. The Murphy seminormal supplier does not establish these semistandard identities, which are essential to the determinant norm. Needed: explicit maps and scalar/triangularity proofs covering all same-label standardizations, corresponding to Mathas Lemmas 5.13–5.17 and Theorem 5.18.

The zero-form argument asserts the row-intersection factorial factor, beta-dominance implication and fixed-row straightening without supplying the required identities. The opened suppliers establish bases and straightening, not this common Gram-entry divisor. Needed: a proved divisibility lemma or explicit Gram-entry calculations for (3,2) and (3,1,1). Independently checked hook valuations, balanced symbols and tableau counts do not establish the vanishing forms used in 3.1.
